### Using Census Tracts as a unit of analysis (with no cutoffs for the large CT)




### Constucting Samples: Household without children and Household with children
## =============================================================================
## Tour-level Activity Space Construction (Hasanzadeh et al. 2017 approach)
## NHTS 2017 | Caregiver travel with/without children
##
## Geographic resolution: Census block-group centroids (from Census TIGER)
## Activity space: Minimum Convex Polygon (MCP)
##   - Home location buffered 100 m
##   - All other stops buffered 100 m
##   - Union of buffers → MCP (convex hull)
## Outcome: log(area in km²) at the tour level
##
## Required NHTS files (assumed in data_dir):
##   hhctbg.csv      — household home BG
##   tripctbg.csv    — per-trip origin/destination BG
##   trippub.csv     — trip public file (tour ID, child accompaniment flags)
##   hhpub.csv       — household public file (household-level controls)
##   perpub.csv      — person public file (person-level controls)
## =============================================================================


```{r include=FALSE}
library(tidyverse)
library(sf)
library(tigris)   # Census TIGER/Line shapefiles → BG centroids
#library(lwgeom)   # convex hull on sf geometry collections

options(tigris_use_cache = TRUE)
```


```{r}
## ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
## 0. Paths — edit these
## ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
data_dir   <- "C:/Users/ohdaw/OneDrive/Documents/R_Projects/CaregiverActivitySpace/data"          # folder with all NHTS CSVs 
output_dir <- "C:/Users/ohdaw/OneDrive/Documents/R_Projects/CaregiverActivitySpace/results"            # where results are written

## ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
## 1. Load NHTS geographic and trip files
## ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
hhctbg  <- read_csv(file.path(data_dir, "hhctbg.csv"),
                    col_types = cols(.default = "c"))
tripctbg <- read_csv(file.path(data_dir, "tripctbg.csv"),
                     col_types = cols(.default = "c"))
trippub  <- read_csv(file.path(data_dir, "trippub.csv"),
                     col_types = cols(.default = "c"))
hhpub    <- read_csv(file.path(data_dir, "hhpub.csv"),
                     col_types = cols(.default = "c"))
perpub   <- read_csv(file.path(data_dir, "perpub.csv"),
                     col_types = cols(.default = "c"))
```


## ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
## 2. Build household-level child count (numu10inhh)
##    Mirrors the Python logic in us_data_processing_1.rmd:
##      numu10inhh = YOUNGCHILD (ages 0–5 from NHTS HH variable)
##                 + num_5_9   (ages 5–9 counted from perpub roster)
##
##    YOUNGCHILD is a household-level variable already in trippub/perpub.
##    Children under 5 are NOT in the perpub roster; YOUNGCHILD captures them.
##    Children 5–9 ARE in the perpub roster via R_AGE_IMP.
## ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

```{r}
# Count ages 5–9 per household from perpub roster
hh_5_9 <- perpub %>%
  mutate(age = as.integer(R_AGE)) %>%    # perpub uses R_AGE; R_AGE_IMP is only in trippub
  filter(!is.na(age)) %>%
  group_by(HOUSEID) %>%
  summarise(num_5_9 = sum(age >= 5 & age <= 9), .groups = "drop")
 
# YOUNGCHILD: household-level count of ages 0–5, lives in hhpub (not trippub)
hh_youngchild <- hhpub %>%
  select(HOUSEID, YOUNGCHILD) %>%
  distinct(HOUSEID, .keep_all = TRUE) %>%
  mutate(YOUNGCHILD = as.integer(YOUNGCHILD),
         YOUNGCHILD = replace_na(YOUNGCHILD, 0L))
 
# Combine: numu10inhh = YOUNGCHILD + num_5_9
hh_child_count <- hh_youngchild %>%
  left_join(hh_5_9, by = "HOUSEID") %>%
  mutate(
    num_5_9    = replace_na(num_5_9, 0L),
    numu10inhh = YOUNGCHILD + num_5_9
  ) %>%
  select(HOUSEID, YOUNGCHILD, num_5_9, numu10inhh)
```


```{r}
## ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
## 2b. Build household-level child counts across the full 0-17 range
##
##   numu10inhh   = YOUNGCHILD (0-5) + num_5_9   (5-9)   [as before]
##   num_10_17    = count of ages 10-17 from perpub roster
##   total_child_0_17 = numu10inhh + num_10_17
##
##   no_child   : total_child_0_17 == 0   (no children of ANY age 0-17)
##   with_child : numu10inhh >= 1          (has a child 0-9, regardless of
##                whether 10-17 kids are also present)
## ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

# Count ages 10-17 per household from perpub roster
hh_10_17 <- perpub %>%
  mutate(age = as.integer(R_AGE)) %>%
  filter(!is.na(age)) %>%
  group_by(HOUSEID) %>%
  summarise(num_10_17 = sum(age >= 10 & age <= 17), .groups = "drop")

# Combine with your existing numu10inhh (0-9) build
hh_child_count_full <- hh_child_count %>%           # from your original 2b: HOUSEID, YOUNGCHILD, num_5_9, numu10inhh
  left_join(hh_10_17, by = "HOUSEID") %>%
  mutate(
    num_10_17         = replace_na(num_10_17, 0L),
    total_child_0_17  = numu10inhh + num_10_17
  )
```


```{r}
## ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
## 2c. Classify households into comparison groups
##     no_child   : total_child_0_17 == 0   (no kids 0-17 at all)
##     with_child : numu10inhh >= 1          (has a child 0-9; 10-17 kids OK too)
##     (households with only 10-17 kids and no 0-9 kids fall into neither
##      group and are dropped from the comparison sample)
## ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

hh_group <- hh_child_count_full %>%
  mutate(
    child_group = case_when(
      total_child_0_17 == 0 ~ "no_child",
      numu10inhh >= 1       ~ "with_child",
      TRUE                  ~ NA_character_   # only-10-17-kids HHs -> excluded
    )
  )

message("No-child households (0-17 clean):        ",
        sum(hh_group$child_group == "no_child", na.rm = TRUE))
message("With-child households (has child 0-9):    ",
        sum(hh_group$child_group == "with_child", na.rm = TRUE))
message("Excluded (only children 10-17, no 0-9):    ",
        sum(is.na(hh_group$child_group) & hh_group$total_child_0_17 > 0))
```


```{r}
## ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
## 2c. Pull household-level control variables (from hhpub)
##     - NUMADLT      : number of adults in HH (splits caregiving load)
##     - HHVEHCNT     : household vehicle count
##     - HHFAMINC     : household income category
##     - HHSIZE       : total household size (to flag other dependents)
##     - URBRUR       : urbanicity (01 urban / 02 suburban-cluster / 03 rural)
##     - MSACAT       : metro status
##     - HH_CBSA      : CBSA code (for FE if needed)
##     - LIF_CYC      : life-cycle category (can help flag elderly/other deps)
## ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

hh_controls <- hhpub %>%
  select(HOUSEID, NUMADLT, HHVEHCNT, HHFAMINC, HHSIZE,
         URBRUR, MSACAT, HH_CBSA, LIF_CYC) %>%
  distinct(HOUSEID, .keep_all = TRUE) %>%
  mutate(
    NUMADLT   = as.integer(NUMADLT),
    HHVEHCNT  = as.integer(HHVEHCNT),
    HHSIZE    = as.integer(HHSIZE),
    veh_per_adult = if_else(NUMADLT > 0, HHVEHCNT / NUMADLT, NA_real_)
  )
```


```{r}
## ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
## 2d. Flag presence of other dependents (older kids 10-15, or elderly)
##     so the "no_child" group isn't silently contaminated by other
##     caregiving obligations. Adjust age bands to whatever perpub allows.
## ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

hh_other_deps <- perpub %>%
  mutate(age = as.integer(R_AGE)) %>%
  filter(!is.na(age)) %>%
  group_by(HOUSEID) %>%
  summarise(
    has_child_10_15 = any(age >= 10 & age <= 15, na.rm = TRUE),
    has_elderly_70p = any(age >= 70, na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = "drop"
  )
```


```{r}
## ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
## 2e. Combine into a single household-level comparison frame
## ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

hh_compare <- hh_group %>%
  left_join(hh_controls,    by = "HOUSEID") %>%
  left_join(hh_other_deps,  by = "HOUSEID") %>%
  mutate(
    has_child_10_15 = replace_na(has_child_10_15, FALSE),
    has_elderly_70p = replace_na(has_elderly_70p, FALSE)
  ) %>%
  filter(child_group %in% c("no_child", "with_child"))

## Optional: drop no_child households that actually have other dependents,
## so "no_child" means no caregiving-relevant dependents at all
hh_compare_clean <- hh_compare %>%
  filter(!(child_group == "no_child" & (has_child_10_15 | has_elderly_70p)))

message("Clean no-child HHs (no other dependents): ",
        sum(hh_compare_clean$child_group == "no_child"))
message("With-child HHs: ",
        sum(hh_compare_clean$child_group == "with_child"))
```


```{r}
## ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
## 3. Restrict to adult respondents (23-69) and attach person-level controls
##    - R_AGE_IMP, R_SEX_IMP : age, sex
##    - WORKER               : employment status
##    - TDWKND (from trippub, joined later at trip level): weekday/weekend
## ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

person_core <- perpub %>%
  mutate(age = as.integer(R_AGE)) %>%
  filter(age >= 23, age <= 69) %>%
  select(HOUSEID, PERSONID, R_AGE = age, R_SEX_IMP, WORKER) %>%
  inner_join(hh_compare_clean, by = "HOUSEID")

message("Adult respondents in comparison sample: ", nrow(person_core))
message("  no_child: ",   sum(person_core$child_group == "no_child"))
message("  with_child: ", sum(person_core$child_group == "with_child"))

## Quick balance check across groups before you go further
person_core %>%
  group_by(child_group) %>%
  summarise(
    n              = n(),
    mean_age       = mean(R_AGE, na.rm = TRUE),
    pct_worker     = mean(WORKER == "01", na.rm = TRUE),
    mean_hhfaminc  = mean(as.integer(HHFAMINC), na.rm = TRUE),
    mean_veh_adult = mean(veh_per_adult, na.rm = TRUE),
    pct_urban      = mean(URBRUR == "01", na.rm = TRUE)
  )
```




### Constucting Activity Spaces
## =============================================================================
## Daily (person-level) Activity Space — No-child vs With-child(0-9) households
## Buffers built from ACTUAL block group polygons, not centroids
## Home -> 100 m buffer around BG polygon boundary
## Each destination -> 100 m buffer around its BG polygon boundary
## Union all buffers (dedup by GEOID) -> convex hull -> area in km^2
## CRS: EPSG:5070 (NAD83 Conus Albers, metres, equal area)
## =============================================================================


```{r}
## ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
## 0. Restrict trip_core to the two comparison groups (not caregiver_hh)
## ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
compare_hh_ids <- hh_compare_clean$HOUSEID   # no_child + with_child households

trip_core_cmp <- trippub %>%
  filter(
    HOUSEID %in% compare_hh_ids,
    as.integer(R_AGE_IMP) >= 23,
    as.integer(R_AGE_IMP) <= 69
  ) %>%
  select(
    HOUSEID, PERSONID, TDTRPNUM,
    WHYTO, WHYFROM, TDWKND, TRAVDAY,
    R_AGE_IMP, R_SEX_IMP, DRIVER, WORKER,
    HHVEHCNT, HHFAMINC, HHSIZE, NUMADLT, LIF_CYC,
    URBRUR, MSACAT, HH_CBSA, WTTRDFIN
  ) %>%
  mutate(trip_num = as.integer(TDTRPNUM)) %>%
  arrange(HOUSEID, PERSONID, trip_num)

## Attach the household group label
trip_core_cmp <- trip_core_cmp %>%
  left_join(hh_group %>% select(HOUSEID, child_group), by = "HOUSEID") %>%
  filter(!is.na(child_group))
```


```{r}
## ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
## 1. Build GEOIDs for home and destinations (same construction as before)
## ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
hhctbg_geo <- hhctbg %>%
  mutate(
    home_geoid = paste0(
      str_pad(HHSTFIPS, 2, "left", "0"),
      str_pad(HHCNTYFP, 3, "left", "0"),
      str_pad(HHCT,     6, "left", "0"),
      str_pad(HHBG,     1, "left", "0")
    )
  ) %>%
  select(HOUSEID, home_geoid) %>%
  filter(HOUSEID %in% compare_hh_ids)

tripctbg_geo <- tripctbg %>%
  filter(DEST_COUNTRY == "USA") %>%
  mutate(
    dest_geoid = paste0(
      str_pad(DEST_ST,   2, "left", "0"),
      str_pad(DEST_CNTY, 3, "left", "0"),
      str_pad(DEST_CT,   6, "left", "0"),
      str_pad(DEST_BG,   1, "left", "0")
    )
  ) %>%
  select(HOUSEID, PERSONID, TDTRPNUM, dest_geoid) %>%
  filter(HOUSEID %in% compare_hh_ids)
```


```{r}
## ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
## 2a. Download ACTUAL block group polygons (UNBUFFERED)
##    Kept only because `bg_area` (BG-size cutoff analysis, later in this file)
##    needs true polygon geometry to measure real BG size.
##    NOT used for activity space anymore — that now comes from bg_centroids.
## ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
all_geoids  <- union(hhctbg_geo$home_geoid, tripctbg_geo$dest_geoid)
state_codes <- unique(substr(all_geoids, 1, 2))

message("Downloading Census BG polygons for ", length(state_codes), " states ...")

## Local cache so reruns in this/future sessions are fast
local_cache <- "C:/tigris_cache"
dir.create(local_cache, showWarnings = FALSE)
options(tigris_use_cache = TRUE, tigris_cache_dir = local_cache)

bg_poly_sf <- map_dfr(state_codes, function(st) {
  message("  Fetching state: ", st)
  out <- tryCatch(
    block_groups(state = st, year = 2017, progress_bar = FALSE) %>%
      select(GEOID),
    error = function(e) {
      message("    FAILED for state ", st, ": ", conditionMessage(e))
      NULL
    }
  )
  message("    -> rows: ", if (is.null(out)) 0 else nrow(out))
  out
})

if (nrow(bg_poly_sf) == 0) {
  stop("bg_poly_sf is empty — no states downloaded successfully. ",
       "Check tempdir()/TMPDIR before continuing.")
}

message("Total BG polygons downloaded across all states: ", nrow(bg_poly_sf))

## Define the projected CRS (NAD83 / Conus Albers, metres, equal area)
## Reused later for bg_area AND for the centroid buffering step
CRS_PROJ <- 5070

bg_poly_matched <- bg_poly_sf %>%
  filter(GEOID %in% all_geoids) %>%
  st_transform(CRS_PROJ)

message("BG polygons matched: ", nrow(bg_poly_matched), " of ", length(all_geoids))
```


```{r}
## ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
## 2b. Download Census BG centroids (home + destination BGs, compare sample)
## ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
message("Downloading Census BG centroids for ", length(state_codes), " states ...")

bg_centroid_sf <- map_dfr(state_codes, function(st) {
  tryCatch(
    block_groups(state = st, year = 2017, progress_bar = FALSE) %>%
      select(GEOID) %>%
      st_centroid(),
    error = function(e) {
      message("    FAILED for state ", st, ": ", conditionMessage(e))
      NULL
    }
  )
})

bg_centroids <- bg_centroid_sf %>%
  filter(GEOID %in% all_geoids) %>%
  st_transform(4326) %>%
  mutate(
    lon = st_coordinates(.)[, 1],
    lat = st_coordinates(.)[, 2]
  ) %>%
  st_drop_geometry()

message("Centroids matched: ", nrow(bg_centroids), " of ", length(all_geoids), " BGs")
```


```{r}
## ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
## 3a. Assemble home + destination GEOIDs per person-day, tagged by role
##    (role determines buffer distance: home = 500 m, destination = 140 m)
## ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
person_home_geoid <- hhctbg_geo   # HOUSEID -> home_geoid

person_dest_geoids <- trip_core_cmp %>%
  select(HOUSEID, PERSONID, TDTRPNUM) %>%
  left_join(tripctbg_geo, by = c("HOUSEID", "PERSONID", "TDTRPNUM")) %>%
  filter(!is.na(dest_geoid)) %>%
  distinct(HOUSEID, PERSONID, dest_geoid) %>%
  rename(geoid = dest_geoid) %>%
  mutate(role = "dest")

person_home_only <- trip_core_cmp %>%
  distinct(HOUSEID, PERSONID) %>%
  left_join(person_home_geoid, by = "HOUSEID") %>%
  rename(geoid = home_geoid) %>%
  filter(!is.na(geoid)) %>%
  mutate(role = "home")

## Keep home and dest rows separate even when the same GEOID appears in both
## roles for a person-day — this way the home point still gets its 500 m
## buffer regardless of whether that BG was also visited as a destination.
person_day_geoids <- bind_rows(person_home_only, person_dest_geoids) %>%
  distinct(HOUSEID, PERSONID, geoid, role)

message("Person-days to process: ",
        n_distinct(paste(person_day_geoids$HOUSEID, person_day_geoids$PERSONID)))
```


```{r}
## Right after section 3a (where person_day_geoids is first built with role)
## Give it a distinct name so it can't be overwritten by section 5's later
## rebuild of "person_day_geoids" (which drops the role column).
person_day_geoids_roles <- person_day_geoids

## ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
## 3a.1-roles (self-contained rebuild). Independent of person_home_only /
##     person_dest_geoids, which get reassigned later in section 5 and are
##     no longer safe to rely on. Rebuilds directly from hhctbg_geo /
##     tripctbg_geo / trip_core_cmp, the original raw sources.
## ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
stopifnot(exists("hhctbg_geo"), exists("tripctbg_geo"), exists("trip_core_cmp"))

person_home_only_roles <- trip_core_cmp %>%
  distinct(HOUSEID, PERSONID) %>%
  left_join(hhctbg_geo, by = "HOUSEID") %>%     # HOUSEID -> home_geoid
  rename(geoid = home_geoid) %>%
  filter(!is.na(geoid)) %>%
  mutate(role = "home")

person_dest_geoids_roles <- trip_core_cmp %>%
  select(HOUSEID, PERSONID, TDTRPNUM) %>%
  left_join(tripctbg_geo, by = c("HOUSEID", "PERSONID", "TDTRPNUM")) %>%
  filter(!is.na(dest_geoid)) %>%
  distinct(HOUSEID, PERSONID, dest_geoid) %>%
  rename(geoid = dest_geoid) %>%
  mutate(role = "dest")

person_day_geoids_roles <- bind_rows(person_home_only_roles, person_dest_geoids_roles) %>%
  distinct(HOUSEID, PERSONID, geoid, role)

message("Person-days to process (role-tagged, rebuilt fresh): ",
        n_distinct(paste(person_day_geoids_roles$HOUSEID, person_day_geoids_roles$PERSONID)))

stopifnot("role" %in% names(person_day_geoids_roles))
stopifnot(all(person_day_geoids_roles$role %in% c("home", "dest")))
```


```{r}
## ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
## 3b. Restrict to CBGs ≤ 1 km² before building activity spaces
##     Uses bg_poly_matched (unbuffered, already in CRS_PROJ) to get true area.
##     Any GEOID > 1 km² is dropped from bg_centroids entirely, so it can no
##     longer contribute a home or destination point to the daily MCP.
##     IMPORTANT: rebuild bg_centroids from the raw centroid source first,
##     so this section is idempotent (safe to re-run without stale state).
## ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

# Rebuild bg_centroids from bg_centroid_sf (the raw, unfiltered centroids
# from section 2b) instead of reusing a possibly-already-filtered object
bg_centroids <- bg_centroid_sf %>%
  filter(GEOID %in% all_geoids) %>%
  st_transform(4326) %>%
  mutate(
    lon = st_coordinates(.)[, 1],
    lat = st_coordinates(.)[, 2]
  ) %>%
  st_drop_geometry()

message("BGs before size cutoff: ", nrow(bg_centroids))
## should now print 91102

bg_area_lookup <- bg_poly_matched %>%
  mutate(area_km2 = as.numeric(st_area(geometry)) / 1e6) %>%
  st_drop_geometry() %>%
  select(GEOID, area_km2)

bg_centroids <- bg_centroids %>%
  left_join(bg_area_lookup, by = "GEOID") %>%
  filter(!is.na(area_km2), area_km2 <= 1)

message("BGs after size cutoff (<= 1 km^2): ", nrow(bg_centroids))
## should print 34942
```


```{r}
## ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
## 3c. Restrict to person-days where HOME *and* ALL destination CBGs
##     are <= 1 km^2. Uses person_day_geoids_roles (the role-tagged table
##     from 3a) so it's unaffected by section 5's later reuse of the
##     person_day_geoids name.
## ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
message("Person-days before full size restriction: ",
        n_distinct(paste(person_day_geoids_roles$HOUSEID, person_day_geoids_roles$PERSONID)))

person_day_geoids_roles <- person_day_geoids_roles %>%
  mutate(bg_ok = geoid %in% bg_centroids$GEOID)

person_day_size_ok <- person_day_geoids_roles %>%
  group_by(HOUSEID, PERSONID) %>%
  summarise(
    n_geoids       = n(),
    n_oversized    = sum(!bg_ok),
    all_geoids_ok  = all(bg_ok),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

message("Person-days with home AND all destinations <= 1 km^2: ",
        sum(person_day_size_ok$all_geoids_ok),
        " (", round(mean(person_day_size_ok$all_geoids_ok) * 100, 1), "%)")

keep_ids <- person_day_size_ok %>%
  filter(all_geoids_ok) %>%
  select(HOUSEID, PERSONID)

person_day_geoids_sizeok <- person_day_geoids_roles %>%
  semi_join(keep_ids, by = c("HOUSEID", "PERSONID")) %>%
  select(-bg_ok)

message("Person-days remaining for activity-space construction: ",
        n_distinct(paste(person_day_geoids_sizeok$HOUSEID, person_day_geoids_sizeok$PERSONID)))

# Sanity check: confirm role survived
stopifnot("role" %in% names(person_day_geoids_sizeok))
```


```{r}
## ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
## 4a. Compute daily MCP area from BUFFERED CENTROIDS
##    (now using the fully size-restricted-less than 1sqkm- person-day set)
##    Home centroid       -> 500 m buffer
##    Destination centroid(s) -> 140 m buffer
##    Union all buffers -> convex hull -> area in km^2
##    CRS: EPSG:5070 (NAD83 Conus Albers, metres, equal area)
## ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
CRS_PROJ <- 5070

compute_daily_mcp_area_centroid <- function(geoid_vec, role_vec) {
  pts <- tibble(geoid = geoid_vec, role = role_vec) %>%
    left_join(bg_centroids, by = c("geoid" = "GEOID")) %>%
    filter(!is.na(lon), !is.na(lat))

  if (nrow(pts) == 0) return(NA_real_)

  pts_sf <- st_as_sf(pts, coords = c("lon", "lat"), crs = 4326) %>%
    st_transform(CRS_PROJ)

  buf_dist     <- if_else(pts_sf$role == "home", 500, 140)
  pts_buffered <- st_buffer(pts_sf, dist = buf_dist)

  mcp <- st_convex_hull(st_union(pts_buffered))
  as.numeric(st_area(mcp)) / 1e6   # km^2
}

message("Computing daily activity spaces (centroid buffers: home 500 m, dest 140 m) ...")

daily_spaces <- person_day_geoids_sizeok %>%
  group_by(HOUSEID, PERSONID) %>%
  group_modify(~ tibble(
    activity_space_km2 = compute_daily_mcp_area_centroid(.x$geoid, .x$role)
  )) %>%
  ungroup()

message("Daily activity spaces computed: ", nrow(daily_spaces))
```


```{r eval=FALSE, include=FALSE}
## ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
## 4b. What happens to a person-day when its home BG is oversize
## ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
## Flag / drop person-days whose HOME BG didn't survive the size cutoff
home_survived <- person_day_geoids %>%
  filter(role == "home") %>%
  semi_join(bg_centroids, by = c("geoid" = "GEOID")) %>%
  distinct(HOUSEID, PERSONID) %>%
  mutate(home_ok = TRUE)

daily_spaces <- daily_spaces %>%
  left_join(home_survived, by = c("HOUSEID", "PERSONID")) %>%
  mutate(home_ok = replace_na(home_ok, FALSE))

message("Person-days with home BG excluded by size cutoff: ",
        sum(!daily_spaces$home_ok))

daily_spaces <- daily_spaces %>% filter(home_ok)
```


```{r}
## ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
## 5. Assemble the set of GEOIDs visited per person-day (home + all dest stops)
## ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
person_home_geoid <- hhctbg_geo   # HOUSEID -> home_geoid

person_dest_geoids <- trip_core_cmp %>%
  select(HOUSEID, PERSONID, TDTRPNUM) %>%
  left_join(tripctbg_geo, by = c("HOUSEID", "PERSONID", "TDTRPNUM")) %>%
  filter(!is.na(dest_geoid)) %>%
  distinct(HOUSEID, PERSONID, dest_geoid)   # dedup: repeat visits to same BG

person_day_geoids <- person_dest_geoids %>%
  rename(geoid = dest_geoid) %>%
  bind_rows(
    trip_core_cmp %>%
      distinct(HOUSEID, PERSONID) %>%
      left_join(person_home_geoid, by = "HOUSEID") %>%
      rename(geoid = home_geoid) %>%
      filter(!is.na(geoid))
  ) %>%
  distinct(HOUSEID, PERSONID, geoid)

message("Person-days to process: ",
        n_distinct(paste(person_day_geoids$HOUSEID, person_day_geoids$PERSONID)))
```


```{r eval=FALSE, include=FALSE}
## ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
## 5b. Outlier exclusion (same 8-SD rule as original)
## ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
as_mean <- mean(daily_spaces$activity_space_km2, na.rm = TRUE)
as_sd   <- sd(daily_spaces$activity_space_km2,   na.rm = TRUE)
daily_spaces <- daily_spaces %>%
  filter(
    !is.na(activity_space_km2),
    activity_space_km2 <= as_mean + 8 * as_sd
  )
message("Person-days retained after outlier exclusion: ", nrow(daily_spaces))
```


```{r}
## ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
## 6. Assemble daily-level model dataset with controls + group label
## ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
day_summary <- trip_core_cmp %>%
  group_by(HOUSEID, PERSONID) %>%
  summarise(
    n_tours      = n_distinct(paste(HOUSEID, PERSONID)),  # placeholder if you keep tour_id upstream
    n_trips      = n(),
    weekend      = first(TRAVDAY) %in% c("01", "07"),
    age          = as.integer(first(R_AGE_IMP)),
    female       = first(R_SEX_IMP) == "02",
    driver       = first(DRIVER) == "01",
    worker       = first(WORKER) == "01",
    veh_cnt      = as.integer(first(HHVEHCNT)),
    no_vehicle   = first(HHVEHCNT) == "0",
    hh_size      = as.integer(first(HHSIZE)),
    n_adults     = as.integer(first(NUMADLT)),
    income_cat   = first(HHFAMINC),
    lif_cyc      = first(LIF_CYC),
    urbrur       = first(URBRUR),
    msacat       = first(MSACAT),
    wt_trip      = first(WTTRDFIN),
    child_group  = first(child_group),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  left_join(daily_spaces, by = c("HOUSEID", "PERSONID")) %>%
  filter(!is.na(activity_space_km2)) %>%
  mutate(log_as_km2 = log(activity_space_km2))

message("Final daily model dataset: ", nrow(day_summary), " person-days")
day_summary %>% count(child_group)
```




## ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
## 14. Regression models (OLS)
##
## constrains weekday vs. weekend activity spaces differently
## (motivated by the Granada paper's weekday/weekend divergence finding)
## ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

```{r}
## =============================================================================
## 1. Recode HHFAMINC into income quartiles (drop refused/don't know)
## =============================================================================

## NHTS 2017 HHFAMINC codes: 01-11 are ordered income brackets;
## -7 = refused, -8 = don't know, -9 = not ascertained -> all treated as missing
day_summary <- day_summary %>%
  mutate(
    income_num = as.integer(income_cat),
    income_num = if_else(income_num %in% c(-7, -8, -9), NA_integer_, income_num)
  ) %>%
  filter(!is.na(income_num))   # drop refused/don't know/not ascertained

message("Rows after dropping missing/refused income: ", nrow(day_summary))

## Quartile the ORDINAL income category (not dollar values, since HHFAMINC
## is a categorical bracket, not a continuous income figure)
day_summary <- day_summary %>%
  mutate(
    income_quartile = ntile(income_num, 4),
    income_quartile = factor(
      income_quartile,
      levels = 1:4,
      labels = c("Q1_lowest", "Q2", "Q3", "Q4_highest")
    )
  )

table(day_summary$income_quartile, useNA = "ifany")
```


```{r}
## =============================================================================

## =============================================================================

## 2a. Overall descriptives by child_group
desc_by_group <- day_summary %>%
  group_by(child_group) %>%
  summarise(
    n                    = n(),
    mean_activity_km2    = mean(activity_space_km2, na.rm = TRUE),
    median_activity_km2  = median(activity_space_km2, na.rm = TRUE),

    mean_hh_size         = mean(hh_size, na.rm = TRUE),
    mean_n_adults        = mean(n_adults, na.rm = TRUE),
    pct_weekend          = mean(weekend, na.rm = TRUE),
    pct_urban            = mean(urbrur == "01", na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

print(desc_by_group)
```

```{r}
print(income_by_group)
```

```{r}
## 2c. Activity space by group AND weekday/weekend (for the interaction question)

print(desc_by_group_weekend)
```

```{r}
## =============================================================================
## 3. Regression models (OLS)
## =============================================================================

## Base controls used across all models
## income_quartile, urbrur, msacat as factors; rest as continuous/binary
day_summary <- day_summary %>%
  mutate(
    urbrur  = factor(urbrur),
    age_c  = age - mean(age, na.rm = TRUE),
    age_sq = age_c^2,
    weekend = if (is.logical(weekend)) {
      factor(weekend, levels = c(FALSE, TRUE), labels = c("weekday", "weekend"))
    } else {
      factor(weekend, levels = c("weekday", "weekend"))
    }
  )

## Model 1: main effect of child_group only (unadjusted)
m1_unadjusted <- lm(
  log_as_km2 ~ child_group,
  data = day_summary
)

## Model 2: adjusted for demographic + household controls
m2_adjusted <- lm(
  log_as_km2 ~ child_group + age + age_sq + female + worker + no_vehicle + 
    n_trips + n_adults + income_quartile,
  data = day_summary
)

## Model 3: adjusted + weekend main effect (additive, same slope both days)
m3_weekend_additive <- lm(
  log_as_km2 ~ child_group + weekend + age + age_sq + female + worker + no_vehicle + 
    n_trips + n_adults + income_quartile,
  data = day_summary
)

## Model 4: child_group x weekend INTERACTION
##   This is the model that answers your 4th bullet directly — it lets the
##   child-presence effect on activity space differ between weekday and
##   weekend, rather than assuming the same effect size applies to both.
m4_weekend_interaction <- lm(
  log_as_km2 ~ child_group * weekend + age + age_sq + female + worker + no_vehicle  + 
    n_trips + n_adults + income_quartile,
  data = day_summary
)

## Compare models
summary(m1_unadjusted)
summary(m2_adjusted)
summary(m3_weekend_additive)
summary(m4_weekend_interaction)

## Formal test: does allowing the interaction significantly improve fit
## over the additive model? (i.e., does the child effect really differ
## by weekday/weekend, or is the additive model sufficient?)
anova(m3_weekend_additive, m4_weekend_interaction)
```


```{r}
## =============================================================================
## 4. Stratified models: weekday-only and weekend-only
##    (alternative to the interaction term — run fully separate models
##     so ALL coefficients, not just child_group, are allowed to differ)
## =============================================================================

m_weekday_only <- lm(
  log_as_km2 ~ child_group + age + female + worker + no_vehicle + n_trips +
    n_adults + income_quartile,
  data = day_summary %>% filter(weekend == "weekday")
)

m_weekend_only <- lm(
  log_as_km2 ~ child_group + age + female + worker + no_vehicle + n_trips +
    n_adults + income_quartile,
  data = day_summary %>% filter(weekend == "weekend")
)

m_weekday_only_interaction <- lm(
  log_as_km2 ~ child_group * female + age + worker + no_vehicle + n_trips +
    n_adults + income_quartile,
  data = day_summary %>% filter(weekend == "weekday")
)

m_weekend_only_interaction <- lm(
  log_as_km2 ~ child_group * female + age + worker + no_vehicle + n_trips +
    n_adults + income_quartile,
  data = day_summary %>% filter(weekend == "weekend")
)


summary(m_weekday_only)
summary(m_weekend_only)
summary(m_weekday_only_interaction)
summary(m_weekend_only_interaction)
```

```{r}
## Side-by-side comparison of the child_group coefficient across strata
library(broom)
bind_rows(
  tidy(m_weekday_only) %>% mutate(sample = "weekday"),
  tidy(m_weekend_only) %>% mutate(sample = "weekend")
) %>%
  filter(str_detect(term, "child_group")) %>%
  select(sample, term, estimate, std.error, p.value)
```


```{r}
## =============================================================================
## A. Does child presence interact with gender?
##    Tests whether the weekday/child effect is really about mothers
##    specifically, rather than "having a child" uniformly across sexes.
## =============================================================================

m5_child_gender_interaction <- lm(
  log_as_km2 ~ child_group * female + weekend + age + age_sq + worker +
    no_vehicle + n_trips + n_adults + income_quartile,
  data = day_summary
)

summary(m5_child_gender_interaction)

## Does adding the interaction improve fit over the additive model (m3)?
anova(m3_weekend_additive, m5_child_gender_interaction)


## =============================================================================
## B. Full three-way: child_group x female x weekend
##    Tests whether the mother-specific constraint (if any) is itself
##    concentrated on weekdays.
## =============================================================================

m6_full_interaction <- lm(
  log_as_km2 ~ child_group * female * weekend + age + age_sq + worker +
    no_vehicle + n_trips + n_adults + income_quartile,
  data = day_summary
)

summary(m6_full_interaction)

anova(m5_child_gender_interaction, m6_full_interaction)


## =============================================================================
## C. Is n_trips mediating the child effect?
##    Compare child_group's coefficient WITH vs WITHOUT controlling for
##    number of trips. If child_group becomes larger/significant once
##    n_trips is dropped, that suggests children affect activity space
##    primarily by changing how much someone travels, not independently
##    of trip frequency.
## =============================================================================

m2_no_trips <- lm(
  log_as_km2 ~ child_group + age + age_sq + female + worker + no_vehicle +
    n_adults + income_quartile,
  data = day_summary
)

m2_with_trips <- lm(
  log_as_km2 ~ child_group + age + age_sq + female + worker + no_vehicle +
    n_trips + n_adults + income_quartile,
  data = day_summary
)

summary(m2_no_trips)
summary(m2_with_trips)

## Side-by-side comparison of just the child_group coefficient across both
bind_rows(
  broom::tidy(m2_no_trips)   %>% mutate(model = "without n_trips"),
  broom::tidy(m2_with_trips) %>% mutate(model = "with n_trips")
) %>%
  filter(term == "child_groupwith_child") %>%
  select(model, term, estimate, std.error, p.value)
```


```{r}
## Proper nested comparison: same covariates as m5, minus the interaction term
m5_additive_only <- lm(
  log_as_km2 ~ child_group + female + weekend + age + age_sq + worker +
    no_vehicle + n_trips + n_adults + income_quartile,
  data = day_summary
)

## Now this isolates the interaction term's contribution correctly
anova(m5_additive_only, m5_child_gender_interaction)
```

```{r}
library(ggeffects)  # or emmeans
library(ggplot2)

## Convert logical predictors to factors before refitting
day_summary <- day_summary %>%
  mutate(
    female     = factor(female,     levels = c(FALSE, TRUE)),
    worker     = factor(worker,     levels = c(FALSE, TRUE)),
    no_vehicle = factor(no_vehicle, levels = c(FALSE, TRUE))
  )

## Refit m7 on the factor-converted data
m7_with_adults_interaction <- lm(
  log_as_km2 ~ child_group * female + child_group * n_adults + weekend +
    age + age_sq + worker + no_vehicle + n_trips + income_quartile,
  data = day_summary
)

## Predicted log_as_km2 at realistic n_adults values, by child_group
predictions <- ggpredict(m7_with_adults_interaction,
                          terms = c("n_adults [1,2,3]", "child_group"))
plot(predictions) +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = c(1, 2, 3))

print(predictions)
```

```{r}
## ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
## Stratified models: weekday and weekend, each with child_group x female
## and child_group x n_adults interactions
## ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
m7_weekday <- lm(
  log_as_km2 ~ child_group * female + child_group * n_adults +
    age + age_sq + worker + no_vehicle + n_trips + income_quartile,
  data = day_summary %>% filter(weekend == "weekday")
)

m7_weekend <- lm(
  log_as_km2 ~ child_group * female + child_group * n_adults +
    age + age_sq + worker + no_vehicle + n_trips + income_quartile,
  data = day_summary %>% filter(weekend == "weekend")
)

summary(m7_weekday)
summary(m7_weekend)


## ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
## Predicted values: n_adults x child_group, faceted by female, for each
## weekday/weekend model separately
## ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
pred_weekday <- ggpredict(m7_weekday,
                           terms = c("n_adults [1,2,3]", "child_group", "female")) %>%
  as.data.frame() %>%
  mutate(period = "Weekday")

pred_weekend <- ggpredict(m7_weekend,
                           terms = c("n_adults [1,2,3]", "child_group", "female")) %>%
  as.data.frame() %>%
  mutate(period = "Weekend")

pred_combined <- bind_rows(pred_weekday, pred_weekend) %>%
  rename(n_adults = x, child_group = group, female = facet)

## Relabel female facet for readability (TRUE/FALSE -> Women/Men)
pred_combined <- pred_combined %>%
  mutate(
    gender_label = if_else(female == "TRUE", "Women", "Men"),
    period       = factor(period, levels = c("Weekday", "Weekend"))
  )

## ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
## 2x2 faceted plot: rows = weekday/weekend, columns = men/women,
## color = child_group
## ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
ggplot(pred_combined, aes(x = n_adults, y = predicted, color = child_group, fill = child_group)) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 1) +
  geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = conf.low, ymax = conf.high), alpha = 0.2, color = NA) +
  facet_grid(period ~ gender_label) +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = c(1, 2, 3)) +
  labs(
    x = "Number of adults in household",
    y = "Predicted log(activity space, km²)",
    color = "Child group",
    fill  = "Child group"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()
```

```{r}
## 3. Descriptive stats split by home vs. destination block groups

  hhctbg_geo %>% transmute(GEOID = home_geoid, role = "home"),
  tripctbg_geo %>% transmute(GEOID = dest_geoid, role = "destination")
```

```{r}
  theme_minimal()
```

```{r}
## Percentile table to help decide on a cutoff
quantile(
  bg_area$area_km2,
  probs = c(0.50, 0.75, 0.90, 0.95, 0.975, 0.99, 0.995, 0.999, 1),
  na.rm = TRUE
)

## How many/what % of block groups would be excluded at various cutoffs
purrr::map_dfr(c(3, 5, 10, 50, 100, 200, 500, 1000, 2000, 5000), function(cutoff) {
  tibble(
    cutoff_km2 = cutoff,
    n_excluded = sum(bg_area$area_km2 > cutoff, na.rm = TRUE),
    pct_excluded = mean(bg_area$area_km2 > cutoff, na.rm = TRUE) * 100
  )
})
```

```{r}
## =============================================================================
## % of person-days (individuals) excluded at various cutoffs
## Excludes a person-day if ANY of their visited GEOIDs (home OR destination)
## exceeds the cutoff
## =============================================================================

## 1. Attach block group area to every (HOUSEID, PERSONID, geoid) row
person_day_area <- person_day_geoids %>%
  left_join(bg_area %>% select(GEOID, area_km2), by = c("geoid" = "GEOID"))

message("Rows with missing area (no BG match): ",
        sum(is.na(person_day_area$area_km2)))

## 2. Get the MAX block group area touched by each person-day
##    (home OR any destination — whichever is largest determines exclusion)
person_day_max_area <- person_day_area %>%
  group_by(HOUSEID, PERSONID) %>%
  summarise(
    max_area_km2 = max(area_km2, na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

total_person_days <- nrow(person_day_max_area)
message("Total person-days: ", total_person_days)

## 3. Compute % excluded at each cutoff
cutoffs <- c(3, 5, 10, 50, 100, 200, 500, 1000, 2000, 5000)

exclusion_by_cutoff <- purrr::map_dfr(cutoffs, function(cutoff) {
  n_excl <- sum(person_day_max_area$max_area_km2 > cutoff, na.rm = TRUE)
  tibble(
    cutoff_km2      = cutoff,
    n_excluded      = n_excl,
    pct_excluded    = n_excl / total_person_days * 100,
    n_remaining     = total_person_days - n_excl,
    pct_remaining   = (total_person_days - n_excl) / total_person_days * 100
  )
})

print(exclusion_by_cutoff)
```

```{r}
urban_bg_area <- bg_area %>%

)

## % excluded at various cutoffs, WITHIN urban BGs only
purrr::map_dfr(c(1, 2, 3, 5, 10, 20, 50, 100), function(cutoff) {

  )
})
```

## =============================================================================
## Build alternativ sample: home BG area <= 5 km^2, no missing covariates
## =============================================================================

```{r}
## 1. Attach home block group area to day_summary
home_area_lookup <- hhctbg_geo %>%
  left_join(bg_area %>% select(GEOID, area_km2), by = c("home_geoid" = "GEOID")) %>%
  rename(home_area_km2 = area_km2) %>%
  select(HOUSEID, home_area_km2)

day_summary_final <- day_summary %>%
  left_join(home_area_lookup, by = "HOUSEID")

message("Person-days before any filtering: ", nrow(day_summary_final))

## 2. Apply the block group size cutoff (home BG <= 5 km^2)
day_summary_final <- day_summary_final %>%
  filter(!is.na(home_area_km2), home_area_km2 <= 5)

message("Person-days after BG size cutoff (<= 5 km^2): ", nrow(day_summary_final))

## 3. Drop any row with missing values in the required covariates
required_vars <- c(
  "child_group", "age", "female", "worker", "no_vehicle",
  "hh_size", "n_adults", "income_quartile", "msacat"
)

n_before_na_drop <- nrow(day_summary_final)

day_summary_final <- day_summary_final %>%
  filter(if_all(all_of(required_vars), ~ !is.na(.)))

message("Person-days after dropping missing covariates: ", nrow(day_summary_final),
        " (dropped ", n_before_na_drop - nrow(day_summary_final), " for missingness)")
```


```{r}
## 4. Final sample size by child_group
final_group_counts <- day_summary_final %>%
  count(child_group) %>%
  mutate(pct = n / sum(n) * 100)

print(final_group_counts)
```


=============================================================================
## Bar chart: distribution of CBG sizes by discrete bins
## =============================================================================

```{r}
## 1. Define bins (aligned with the cutoffs you're already testing)
bg_area_binned <- bg_area %>%
  mutate(
    size_bin = cut(
      area_km2,
      breaks = c(0, 1, 3, 5, 10, 20, 50, 100, 200, 500, 1000, Inf),
      labels = c("<1", "1-3", "3-5", "5-10", "10-20", "20-50",
                 "50-100", "100-200", "200-500", "500-1000", ">1000"),
      right = TRUE
    )
  )

## 2. Count + percentage per bin
bin_counts <- bg_area_binned %>%
  count(size_bin) %>%
  mutate(pct = n / sum(n) * 100)

print(bin_counts)

## 3. Bar chart
ggplot(bin_counts, aes(x = size_bin, y = n)) +
  geom_col(fill = "steelblue") +
  geom_text(aes(label = paste0(round(pct, 1), "%")), vjust = -0.3, size = 3) +
  labs(
    title = "Distribution of Census Block Group Sizes",
    x = "Block group area (km^2)",
    y = "Count"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()
```
